definition: Lowest launch price per kg to low Earth orbit of any operational vehicle in the obs year (list price / full-payload basis, as reported)

THE rockets KPI: lowest price per kg to low Earth orbit of a dedicated launch among the rockets in service in the obs year, in constant 2025 US$ (BLS CPI-U). Computed by collectors/rockets.py: a rocket's price = its published list price / the LEO capacity published with it (list-price-* and list-leo-kg-* in this registry), deflated with the obs year's CPI; after its last listed year it is held in real terms; a published-price / maximum-capacity proxy, not a quoted offer to carry that mass; rockets without list prices use the CSIS Aerospace Security Project $/kg (CSIS's estimate of a dedicated launch at its first successful launch / full LEO payload, FY2021 $, via Our World in Data) moved to 2025 $ with CPI. In service from the first successful launch (CSIS's year) through the last orbital or deep-space launch in JSR GCAT (to date if within the last 3 years). Replaces cost-to-leo-best (nominal prices as reported).
